mainEntity.name: How can you evidence minors’ data / LGPD Art. 14 in folders and spreadsheets without coding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a local discovery tool that scans the folders and files you point it at (spreadsheets, CSVs, exports), identifies columns and values that suggest age or date of birth, and flags signals of possible minors’ data with high priority in the report. DataBoar does this offline, with no DBA or API needed, and produces Excel (for people) and JSON (for machines). These are inventory and triage signals — not legal age verification or a legal opinion.

mainEntity.name: What is differential treatment under LGPD Art. 14 in this context?

acceptedAnswer.text: LGPD Art. 14 deals with the consent and processing of children’s and adolescents’ data with heightened care. In the product, “differential treatment” means prioritizing and highlighting in the report signals of possible minors’ data (for example DOB_POSSIBLE_MINOR), cross-referenced with identifiers in the same folder or table — for the DPO or controller to triage. The tool does not decide whether parental consent is valid.

mainEntity.name: Does the tool generate the report on its own?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, once you point it at the target (a folder or a config). The scan produces a findings spreadsheet and prioritized recommendations. You check the paths; policy, legal basis, and any response to the ANPD stay with the organization.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a programmer, a DBA, or an API to find a school record or an LMS export?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for the file path. LMS CSV/Excel exports, enrollment folders, and class spreadsheets can be pointed at as a filesystem target. A database is optional and configurable later. Start with the demo on synthetic data on Windows, without Docker.

faq.html.title: FAQ — Personal-data inventory and discovery (LGPD) | DataBoar
faq.html.description: Frequently asked questions about personal-data inventory, LGPD data discovery, installing on Windows without Docker, local open source, and Excel reports. Clear answers for firms, SMEs, and people outside IT.
faq.html.og:title: FAQ — Personal-data inventory and discovery (LGPD) | DataBoar
faq.html.og:description: Clear answers: what a personal-data inventory is, how to find where your company’s data is, whether you need IT, Docker, or a DPO, and how to start on Windows.

mainEntity.name: What is a personal-data inventory under the LGPD?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the record of which personal data the organization processes, where it is stored, for what purpose, under which legal basis, who has access, and for how long. The LGPD (Art. 37) requires controllers and processors to keep a record of processing operations. Without an inventory it is hard to answer data subjects, prepare a DPIA/RIPD, or demonstrate compliance.

mainEntity.name: How do I find where my company’s personal data is?

acceptedAnswer.text: Beyond interviewing teams and filling in spreadsheets, you can automate technical discovery: scan folders, files (PDF, Excel, Word, ZIP) and, in many cases, databases and systems, identifying CPF, email, bank details, and other patterns. DataBoar does this discovery locally (the data does not leave your machine) and produces an Excel report with the findings.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to be in IT or have a DPO to use DataBoar?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. There is a path built for people who have never used a terminal: a demo on Windows without Docker, with explained steps. Micro-enterprises and solo professionals are often not required to appoint a DPO (ANPD Resolution CD/ANPD No. 2/2022). DataBoar produces technical evidence; the compliance decision stays with the person responsible for the organization.

mainEntity.name: Does DataBoar send my data to the cloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The model is local-first: the scan runs in your environment. Only metadata and structured findings are produced as a report; the contents of client files are not sent to third-party servers.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to install Docker?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Docker is an option for people who already use containers. On Windows there is a native path with Python and the demo command data-boar --demo, described step by step on the Windows without Docker page.

mainEntity.name: What are the ways to install DataBoar?

acceptedAnswer.text: From PyPI: pip, pipx, or uvx data-boar --demo (a demo on synthetic data), on Linux, Windows, and macOS (installation validated in GitHub Actions CI); on Windows, the Windows without Docker guide walks through the pipx steps. There is also a Docker Hub image and native packages (deb, rpm, apk, pacman) attached to every release. The MSI installer for Windows is in progress.

mainEntity.name: Does it work with ZIP files and password-protected files?

acceptedAnswer.text: ZIP files are analyzed from the inside, without you having to unpack folder by folder. Password-protected files cannot have their contents read (that is the password’s job); the report records that reading was blocked, so you know which documents are already locked.

mainEntity.name: Is DataBoar free?

acceptedAnswer.text: The open source core is free and the code is public on GitHub. The model is open-core: the base stays open and auditable; advanced features, support, and SLA for larger corporate environments may be commercial. Smaller firms can start and operate on the free core.

mainEntity.name: Is it only for the LGPD, or also for tax data and other frameworks?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The entry wedge in Brazil is the LGPD (CPF, sensitive data, etc.), but DataBoar is not only for that. The same engine helps discover tax and financial patterns (CNPJ, bank details, etc.) and produce technical evidence aligned with other frameworks — always inventory and triage, not a legal opinion.

mainEntity.name: How do I start without fearing I’ll break the computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Always start with demo mode: data-boar --demo uses only synthetic (fake) data and opens the panel at http://127.0.0.1:8088. None of your real files are touched. Only after validating, point it at a test folder or, with help, at the firm’s real folders.

mainEntity.name: ANPD spreadsheet or automatic tool — which should I use?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ANPD’s simplified spreadsheet helps organize the record of processing activities (the administrative side). It does not scan the disk for a CPF forgotten in an old PDF or spreadsheet. A discovery tool and the spreadsheet complement each other: one finds where the data actually is; the other documents purpose, legal basis, and owners.

mainEntity.name: Does DataBoar replace DPO-as-a-Service or self-declared mapping platforms?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — they are different categories. Outsourced-DPO / self-declared mapping platforms usually document what the organization declares about processes and routines (client data generally does not enter the platform). DataBoar does local technical discovery: it looks for where the data actually appears in folders and files and produces inventory and triage evidence. They complement each other; one does not replace the other. It is not a legal opinion or a compliance seal.

mainEntity.name: How do I find minors’ data in my folders without coding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Point folders and exports (enrollment, LMS, spreadsheets) at a local scan. DataBoar looks for columns and values of age or date of birth and flags signals of possible minors’ data in the Excel/JSON report. No DBA or API is needed for the file path. These are inventory signals — not legal age verification. See the dedicated case: casos/menores-lgpd-art-14.html.

mainEntity.name: What does differential treatment under LGPD Art. 14 mean in discovery?

acceptedAnswer.text: In inventory practice, it means prioritizing and highlighting in the report signals of possible children’s or adolescents’ data (LGPD Art. 14; GDPR Art. 8 parallel), including by cross-referencing identifiers in the same file. The tool does not decide whether the legal guardian’s consent is valid and does not issue an opinion.

mainEntity.name: Does the tool generate the possible-minors report on its own?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, once you point it at the target. The scan produces a spreadsheet and prioritized recommendations; you check the paths. Policy, legal basis, and regulatory response stay with the DPO, legal counsel, and the organization.

mainEntity.name: Can I find a school record or an LMS export without being in IT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes for files: CSV/Excel and export folders can be pointed at without coding. Start with the synthetic demo on Windows without Docker; only then point at a test folder. There is a case guide at casos/menores-lgpd-art-14.html.
